searchText: > Has anyone explored making an on-disk storage format and engine based on our merkle tree design? I think if you make a verkle tree implementation that stores nodes by their position in the tree, and edits them in place, then you can get an implementation where you just need ~4 DB reads (because verkle trees are 256-ary), and then if you assume a few hundred MB of cache, that goes down to ~1 DB read So the problem becomes easier through a combination of (i) in-place editing instead of hash-storage and garbage collection, and (ii) the much greater width of the tree The prover has: * The polynomial P * A coordinate X * A value Y, with the claim that P(X) = Y The verifier already has: * A commitment to P (it's assumed that the verifier knows that the commitment is "legit" because they got it from some other source, eg. because it's hashed into some block that they verified); we'll call this commitment C * X and Y (eg. because the claimed values are provided in a witness, and the protocol here is just verifying that witness) The prover provides a proof. The proof proves that P'(x) = y for *some* P' that matches C. There is only one possible P', which equals P The proof verification algorithm operates over the proof and over C, so the proof is tied to C Thanks! So my issue relates to "The verifier already has a commitment to P" I'm basing myself on https://notes.ethereum.org/@vbuterin/verkle_tree_eip#Verkle-tree-definition and according to there, we only have a commitment to vector values (not to polynomial coefficients such that evaluation of the polynomial returns the value) But I think I found the answer at the bottom of the page here: https://dankradfeist.de/ethereum/cryptography/2021/07/27/inner-product-arguments.html#creating-an-ipa-for-a-polynomial-in-coefficient-form Which to summarize says that: If we have: * `a` a vector of values known by the prover * `P(X)` a polynomial returning the vector value at the position `X` * C, a commitment to `a` trusted by the verifier (e.g.) from a block Then we can prove `a . b = P(X)`, where `b` is a vector derived from `X` and the domain ([0-255] in this case) via the barycentric formula, such that the verifier will indeed be convinced that `P(X)` is the value at index `X` in the vector `a`. So the thing I was really missing was this barycentric formula to get `b` such that the verifier would be able to trust that the proof is consistent with its existing pedersen commitment to the vector. <@!427491045308235776> problem solved (at least for now)

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
> Has anyone explored making an on-disk storage format and engine based on our merkle tree design?

I think if you make a verkle tree implementation that stores nodes by their position in the tree, and edits them in place, then you can get an implementation where you just need ~4 DB reads (because verkle trees are 256-ary), and then if you assume a few hundred MB of cache, that goes down to ~1 DB read

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: So the problem becomes easier through a combination of (i) in-place editing instead of hash-storage and garbage collection, and (ii) the much greater width of the tree

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
The prover has:

* The polynomial P
* A coordinate X
* A value Y, with the claim that P(X) = Y

The verifier already has:

* A commitment to P (it's assumed that the verifier knows that the commitment is "legit" because they got it from some other source, eg. because it's hashed into some block that they verified); we'll call this commitment C
* X and Y (eg. because the claimed values are provided in a witness, and the protocol here is just verifying that witness)

The prover provides a proof. The proof proves that P'(x) = y for *some* P' that matches C. There is only one possible P', which equals P

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: The proof verification algorithm operates over the proof and over C, so the proof is tied to C

excerpts.author: norswap
excerpts.content:
Thanks! So my issue relates to
"The verifier already has a commitment to P"
I'm basing myself on https://notes.ethereum.org/@vbuterin/verkle_tree_eip#Verkle-tree-definition
and according to there, we only have a commitment to vector values (not to polynomial coefficients such that evaluation of the polynomial returns the value)

But I think I found the answer at the bottom of the page here: https://dankradfeist.de/ethereum/cryptography/2021/07/27/inner-product-arguments.html#creating-an-ipa-for-a-polynomial-in-coefficient-form

Which to summarize says that:

If we have:
* `a` a vector of values known by the prover
* `P(X)` a polynomial returning the vector value at the position `X`
* C, a commitment to `a` trusted by the verifier (e.g.) from a block

Then we can prove `a . b = P(X)`, where `b` is a vector derived from `X` and the
domain ([0-255] in this case) via the barycentric formula, such that the
verifier will indeed be convinced that `P(X)` is the value at index `X` in the vector `a`.

So the thing I was really missing was this barycentric formula to get `b` such
that the verifier would be able to trust that the proof is consistent with its
existing pedersen commitment to the vector.

<@!427491045308235776> problem solved (at least for now)
